partners.mechanism_chain: MEFV (HGNC:7027) —INCREASES→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670); NLRP3 (HGNC:11459) —INCREASES→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammation (HP:00114201); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Erythema (HP:0000975); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing loss (HP:0000365). Gain-of-function mutations in MEFV (associated with Familial Mediterranean Fever, a condition with overlapping autoinflammatory features with Sweet Syndrome) and NLRP3 directly lead to hyperactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. This overactivation results in the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, contributing to the characteristic inflammation (e.g., erythema) seen in Sweet syndrome. Aberrant inflammasome activity can also underlie inflammatory processes that may contribute to or exacerbate hearing loss in autosomal dominant hearing loss 34.

partners.mechanism_chain: NLRP3 (HGNC:7938) —DISRUPTS→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032669); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032669) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammatory response (HP:00114210); Inflammatory response (HP:00114210) —LEADS_TO→ Fever (HP:0000141); Inflammatory response (HP:00114210) —LEADS_TO→ Erythema (HP:0011222); Inflammatory response (HP:00114210) —LEADS_TO→ Neutrophilic dermatosis (HP:0030172). #### 1. hearing loss, autosomal dominant 34, with or without inflammation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.490)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-844456, Reactome:R-HSA-9660826)

**Proposed mechanism:** MEFV (HGNC:7027) —INCREASES→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670); NLRP3 (HGNC:11459) —INCREASES→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammation (HP:00114201); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Erythema (HP:0000975); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing loss (HP:0000365). Gain-of-function mutations in MEFV (associated with Familial Mediterranean Fever, a condition with overlapping autoinflammatory features with Sweet Syndrome) and NLRP3 directly lead to hyperactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. This overactivation results in the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, contributing to the characteristic inflammation (e.g., erythema) seen in Sweet syndrome. Aberrant inflammasome activity can also underlie inflammatory processes that may contribute to or exacerbate hearing loss in autosomal dominant hearing loss 34.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any evidence for NLRP3 inflammasome activation or downstream inflammatory markers in patients with either disease, or demonstration that mutations in MEFV and NLRP3 do not lead to increased IL-1beta production in relevant cellular models. _(variant: If common variants within MEFV or NLRP3 (gnomAD allele frequency > 1%) are found to be causative for both conditions without functional evidence of gain-of-function.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway with inhibitors could offer a therapeutic strategy for both the inflammatory manifestations of Sweet syndrome and potentially mitigate the inflammatory component contributing to hearing loss in autosomal dominant hearing loss 34, thereby providing a shared therapeutic avenue.

Gain-of-function mutations in MEFV (associated with Sweet syndrome) and NLRP3 (associated with Muckle-Wells syndrome) both lead to hyperactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, which in turn drives inflammatory processes manifesting as distinct but overlapping phenotypes including neutrophilic dermatosis, recurrent fever, urticaria, and arthralgia.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in MEFV do not lead to increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation, or that mutations in NLRP3 do not lead to increased IL-1beta production and downstream inflammatory phenotypes. _(variant: gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01 for pathogenic variants in MEFV or NLRP3.)_
